title_en: Pinggu Royal Flavor Roast Chicken Factory v. Tang Guoxing — dispute over confirmation of patent application right
keywords_en: civil; dispute over patent application right; second instance; High People's Court; Beijing; legal person; natural person; Patent Law; determination of service invention and non-service invention; ownership of patent application right; validity of patent application right clause in agreement; uphold original judgment; secret family recipe; method of making roast chicken; technology transfer; change of patent application right; patent right; Tang Guoxing confirmation of patent application right dispute
full_text_en:
Pinggu Palace Style Roast Chicken Factory v. Tang Guoxing — Dispute over Confirmation of Patent Application Rights

Plaintiff: Beijing Pinggu Palace Style Roast Chicken Factory.
Legal Representative: Zhang Tijing, Factory Director.

Defendant: Tang Guoxing, male, 59 years old, Technician of Beijing Haidian District Palace Style Roast Food Factory.

The plaintiff, Beijing Pinggu Palace Style Roast Chicken Factory, filed a lawsuit with the Beijing Intermediate People's Court against the defendant, Tang Guoxing, concerning a dispute over the confirmation of patent application rights.

The plaintiff alleged: During the period when the defendant, Tang Guoxing, was employed as the plaintiff's deputy technical director, he developed and perfected "a method for preparing palace style roast chicken" using all material conditions provided by the plaintiff. This method should be considered a service invention-creation, and the patent application right should legally belong to the plaintiff. However, the defendant used forged certificates to apply to the patent administrative authority for a non-service invention-creation. The plaintiff requested the court to confirm the plaintiff as the patent applicant for "a method for preparing palace style roast chicken."

The defendant argued: "A method for preparing palace style roast chicken," which the defendant perfected on the basis of a family secret recipe, is a non-service invention-creation, and the patent application right should rightfully belong to the defendant. Moreover, the patent application right for this method has been formally confirmed to the defendant by the patent administrative authority. Therefore, the defendant requested the court to dismiss the plaintiff's claim.

The Beijing Intermediate People's Court, after trial, found the following facts: "A method for preparing palace style roast chicken" originated from the family secret recipe of the defendant, Tang Guoxing, and was later perfected by the defendant through practice. In March 1985, Pinggu County Daxingzhuang Township, Beijing, signed a contract with Zhonghua New Technology Company for the transfer of "palace style roast chicken" technology. The defendant, as a technician employed by Zhonghua New Technology Company, represented the company in teaching the technology to Daxingzhuang Township. Based on this, Daxingzhuang Township established the Pinggu Palace Style Roast Chicken Factory (the plaintiff in this case, hereinafter referred to as the Roast Chicken Factory). In June 1986, after the employment contract between the defendant and Zhonghua New Technology Company expired, the plaintiff and the defendant entered into an agreement. The agreement stipulated that: the defendant would be responsible for technical training and product quality inspection for the plaintiff, and would provide self-collected medicinal materials and promotional materials; the plaintiff would provide the defendant with treatment equivalent to that of a senior technician, a monthly salary of RMB 300, and free board and lodging; the defendant agreed to have the plaintiff as one of the patent applicants, provided the plaintiff voluntarily paid the patent application fee and application maintenance fee, and would be responsible for handling technology transfer; the defendant agreed to receive 25% of the technology transfer fees handled by the plaintiff, with the remaining 75% to be used as a fund for the plaintiff to handle patent matters; and the patent right would belong to the defendant. On June 13, the plaintiff filed a patent application for "a method for preparing palace style roast chicken" with the China Patent Office. The inventor named on the application was Tang Guoxing, and the applicant was the Roast Chicken Factory. On September 26 of the same year, the plaintiff's then legal representative and factory director, Wang Hongguang, issued a certificate in the name of the plaintiff to the China Patent Office, stating that due to the plaintiff's and defendant's lack of understanding of the relevant legal provisions on patent application rights, the patent applicant was incorrectly listed as the plaintiff, and requested that the patent applicant be changed to Tang Guoxing. Based on the plaintiff's certificate, the China Patent Office changed the patent applicant in the bibliographic data of the patent application from the Roast Chicken Factory to Tang Guoxing. On March 24, 1989, the plaintiff again submitted a certificate from the Pinggu County Public Security Bureau, claiming that after investigation by the public security authorities, "Wang Hongguang and Tang Guoxing have both confessed that the certificate for the change of bibliographic data was forged," and once again requested a change of patent applicant. Based on this certificate, the China Patent Office changed the patent applicant back to the plaintiff. The defendant disagreed with the above change and requested the Beijing Patent Administration Office to mediate the dispute over patent application rights between the defendant and the plaintiff. After mediation, the Beijing Patent Administration Office issued a decision on March 4, 1991, confirming that the patent application right for "a method for preparing palace style roast chicken" belonged to the defendant. The plaintiff disagreed and filed this lawsuit.

The Beijing Intermediate People's Court held: "A method for preparing palace style roast chicken" is a technology perfected by the defendant, Tang Guoxing, on the basis of a family secret recipe. It was precisely because the defendant possessed this technology that the plaintiff signed a contract with Zhonghua New Technology Company to engage the defendant to teach the roast chicken technology. The facts indicate that the defendant had already completed this invention-creation of the method for preparing palace style roast chicken before coming to the plaintiff's factory. The plaintiff's claim that it provided all material conditions for the development and perfection of the method, which should constitute a service invention, is not supported by evidence and cannot be established. Therefore, "a method for preparing palace style roast chicken" is a non-service invention-creation independently completed by the defendant, and the patent application right should belong to the defendant. As for the agreement signed between the plaintiff and the defendant concerning the patent application right and patent right, according to Article 6 and Article 10, Paragraph 1 of the Patent Law, the patent right is only granted to the patent applicant. Only when any unit or individual applies for a patent as a patent applicant can they possibly obtain the patent right. Only if the defendant transfers his patent application right for "a method for preparing palace style roast chicken" to the plaintiff can the plaintiff legally obtain the patent application right and, upon approval of the application, obtain the patent right. In the agreement between the plaintiff and the defendant, there were both provisions that the plaintiff would be one of the patent applicants and provisions that the patent right would belong to the defendant, which is inconsistent with the principle in the Patent Law that the subject of the patent application right and the patent right should be consistent. This indicates that the term "patent applicant" used by both parties in the agreement was a misunderstanding of the concept of "patent applicant" within the meaning of the Patent Law. Shortly after the agreement was signed, the plaintiff's legal representative had already issued a statement to the patent authority declaring that the patent applicant should be Tang Guoxing. Therefore, the patent application right for "a method for preparing palace style roast chicken" should belong to the defendant. As for the issue of the plaintiff, relying on the certificate from the Pinggu County Public Security Bureau, again changing the patent applicant with the China Patent Office, because the dispute between the plaintiff and the defendant is one over the confirmation of patent application rights, which is not within the functions and duties of the public security authorities according to law, and moreover, the statements in that certificate were made by Wang Hongguang and Tang Guoxing under duress from the public security authorities, it cannot be relied upon as evidence. Accordingly, on June 10, 1992, the Beijing Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment: 1. The patent application right for "a method for preparing palace style roast chicken" belongs to the defendant, Tang Guoxing. 2. The plaintiff, the Roast Chicken Factory's claim is dismissed. The litigation cost of RMB 400 shall be borne by the plaintiff, the Roast Chicken Factory.

After the first-instance judgment was announced, the plaintiff, the Roast Chicken Factory, appealed to the Beijing High People's Court. The reasons for appeal were: 1. The "a method for preparing palace style roast chicken" that was the subject of the patent application was already different from the family secret recipe for "palace style roast chicken" of the appellee, Tang Guoxing. This difference is the technical improvement achieved by the appellee using the material conditions provided by the appellant, therefore, this technology should be a service invention-creation. 2. While it is true that both parties had a significant misunderstanding of the Patent Law when signing the agreement, it was not a misunderstanding of the concept of "patent applicant," but rather that the intended wording "right of inventorship belongs to Party A (i.e., Tang Guoxing)" was mistakenly written as "patent right belongs to Party A." Therefore, what should be changed is the provision that "the patent right belongs to Party A."

The appellee, Tang Guoxing, argued: Invention, meaning the creation of new things or new methods, is the exercise of a person's creative ability and is not a manifestation of rights conferred by law. The law never has, and cannot, decide whether to allow or prohibit a person from exercising their creative ability by way of granting rights. A person with creative ability does not need to obtain a so-called "right of inventorship" before exercising their creative ability; a person without such ability, even if granted a so-called "right of inventorship" by law, cannot create new things or new methods. Therefore, the concept of "right of inventorship" has no legal basis and no practical significance. The inventor of "a method for preparing palace style roast chicken" is Tang Guoxing. This fact has been clear from beginning to end and has never been disputed by either party. There was no need to agree on an "inventor" in the agreement, nor did anyone have the right to make such an agreement.

The Beijing High People's Court, after trial, held: In 1985, when the appellee, Tang Guoxing, went to the appellant, the Roast Chicken Factory, to teach the roast chicken technology, the formulation and dosage ratio of the main raw materials used had already been completed. When the patent application was filed, although there were slight changes in this raw material formulation and dosage ratio, there was no essential difference between the two. Therefore, this technology still belongs to the non-service invention-creation independently completed by the appellee. The appellant's claim that it provided all material conditions for the appellee to perfect the production method cannot serve as a reason to establish it as a service invention-creation. Moreover, the "all material conditions" referred to by the appellant include the living benefits provided to the appellee, which were obligations the appellant was required to fulfill under the agreement during the period the appellee was employed to teach the technology. Regarding the appellant's claim that "right of inventorship" was mistakenly written as "patent right," the appellant failed to submit evidence supporting the claim of a mistaken writing, and the parties involved at the time the agreement was signed testified that it was not a mistaken writing. Therefore, the appellant's reasons for appeal are not adopted. The first-instance judgment had clear facts, sufficient evidence, and correct application of law, and should be affirmed. Accordingly, on October 14, 1992, the Beijing High People's Court rendered the following judgment: The appellant, the Roast Chicken Factory's appeal is dismissed, and the first-instance judgment is affirmed.
